hints: Notice that nitric acid is doing two different jobs here, forming the nitrate salt and also being reduced to NO.
Start with 3 Cu atoms, so you must make 3 units of $\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2$ which already locks up 6 nitrate groups.
Add the extra acid needed to supply the N atoms for NO and the H atoms for water, then balance H and check the total.
walkthrough:
**Write the unbalanced skeleton**

Think of this as a recipe with missing numbers. List all the reactants and products first.

$$\text{Cu} + \text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Cu(NO}_3)_2 + \text{NO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Spot the two roles of nitric acid**

This is the key idea. Some $\text{HNO}_3$ provides $\text{NO}_3^-$ for the salt, and some $\text{HNO}_3$ is reduced to $\text{NO}$. That is why you need more than 6 moles.

For 3 Cu, you must form 3 $\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2$, so that uses $3 \times 2 = 6$ N atoms just for the salt.

**Balance Cu, N, H and O together**

Balance Cu first, then use redox or atom counting to finish. The fully balanced equation is:

$$3\text{Cu} + 8\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Check: 3 Cu, 8 H, 8 N and 24 O on both sides. So 8 moles of acid react with 3 moles of copper.

options.A: 2 is the coefficient of NO in the balanced equation, not of $\text{HNO}_3$. It is easy to mix up the product with the reactant if you do not balance fully.
options.B: 4 is the coefficient of water, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, in the balanced equation. It does not represent the moles of acid used.
options.C: 6 counts only the nitrate ions needed to make 3 $\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2$. It forgets the extra 2 $\text{HNO}_3$ molecules that are reduced to form 2 NO and supply H for water.
options.D: 8 is correct. From $3\text{Cu} + 8\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$, 6 moles of acid provide nitrate for the salt and 2 more moles are reduced to NO, giving 8 total.
